obs: "It was contended, by the counsel for the banks, that no law could be regarded as declaring the policy of the state, unless it was penal; and inflicted some punishment for its violation. ... I know of no such- exclusive rule by which to reach the mind and intention of the legislature. If the language used shows clearly that particular acts were intended to be prohibited, and the .act is afterwards done, it is against the policy of the law and void."
"A payment or transfer condemned by the express terms of the Bankrupt Act cannot protect them."
Gibbs v. Consolidated Gas Co. of Baltimore
"Here the contract was directly in the teeth of the statute, which expressly forbade the Equitable Gas-Light Company from entering into it."
